items.body:
## Bug Description

Hermes terminal tool silently loses command output on Chinese Windows due to GBK encoding crash in Python's subprocess reader thread.

## Root Cause

Python's `subprocess` with `text=True` but **without** explicit `encoding='utf-8'` defaults to `locale.getpreferredencoding(False)` → `cp936` (GBK) on Chinese Windows. When command output contains bytes that are not valid GBK (emoji, Unicode symbols, some English tool output), the `_readerthread` crashes silently, and the entire terminal output is lost.

## Evidence

From `~/AppData/Local/hermes/logs/tui_gateway_crash.log`:

```
UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0x94 in position 1137: illegal multibyte sequence
  at subprocess.py, line 1599, in _readerthread
    buffer.append(fh.read())
```

This error appears **187 times** since 2025-06-25.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On Chinese Windows 10/11 (system locale: zh-CN)
2. Run any terminal command that outputs non-GBK characters, e.g.:
   - `npm install -g pptxgenjs` (node progress bars with Unicode spinners)
   - Commands with emoji (e.g. checkmark, rocket)
   - Python output with Unicode characters
3. Observe: `[Result unavailable]` or silent output loss

## Expected Behavior

All command output should be captured and returned reliably, regardless of character encoding.

## Proposed Fix

In the terminal tool implementation, when calling `subprocess.Popen` or `subprocess.run`:

```python
# Instead of:
subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)

# Use:
subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')
```

The `errors='replace'` ensures that even if some bytes can't be decoded as UTF-8, they get replaced with U+FFFD instead of crashing the entire reader thread.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10 (10.0.22621)
- System locale: zh-CN (Chinese Simplified)
- Python: 3.11.15
- Shell: Git Bash (MSYS2)
- Hermes version: latest (as of 2026-07-03)

items.title: forking a session double-encodes the reasoning columns — forked sessions silently lose reasoning replay

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

`get_messages()` returns stored rows with `content` and `tool_calls` hydrated back
into structures, but the three structured reasoning columns —
`reasoning_details`, `codex_reasoning_items`, `codex_message_items` — stay the
raw TEXT the row holds. Any caller that pipes those rows back into a write
re-serializes that TEXT, because both writers (`append_message` and
`_insert_message_rows`) run an unguarded `json.dumps()` on whatever they get.

The fork endpoint does exactly this round-trip. `POST
/api/sessions/{session_id}/fork` copies the source session with
`get_messages()` into `replace_messages()` (`gateway/platforms/api_server.py`
lines 1835-1836), so every reasoning column in the fork ends up holding
`"[{\"type\": ...}]"` (a JSON-encoded *string*) instead of `[{"type": ...}]`
(a JSON array). When the fork is resumed, `get_messages_as_conversation()`
decodes the column once and hands consumers the inner **string** instead of
the original list. Nothing crashes — every consumer gates on
`isinstance(..., list)` — the reasoning context just silently disappears from
the forked conversation. Each further fork wraps one more layer.

## Root Cause

Write side, `hermes_state.py` — both writers assume their input is a live
structure, never the column's own already-serialized TEXT:

```python
# append_message, lines 3127-3138
reasoning_details_json = (
    json.dumps(reasoning_details)
    if reasoning_details else None
)
```

```python
# _insert_message_rows, lines 3235-3243 (shared by replace_messages
# and archive_and_compact per its docstring)
reasoning_details_json = (
    json.dumps(reasoning_details) if reasoning_details else None
)
```

Read side: `get_messages()` (line 3399) hydrates only `content` and
`tool_calls`; the reasoning columns pass through as TEXT. That asymmetry is
fine for read-only callers, but it makes `get_messages()` →
`replace_messages()` an unstable round-trip — and that pair is exactly the
fork handler (`_handle_fork_session`, `api_server.py` lines 1835-1836):

```python
messages = db.get_messages(source_id)
db.replace_messages(fork_id, messages)
```

## What the forked session loses

On resume, `get_messages_as_conversation()` (lines 3798/3804/3810) decodes
each column once and hands the resulting string to consumers that all no-op
on non-lists:

* `agent/anthropic_adapter.py:1791` — `_extract_preserved_thinking_blocks`
  returns `[]` unless `reasoning_details` is a list, so preserved Anthropic
  thinking blocks drop out of replay.
* `agent/codex_responses_adapter.py:381` and `:432` — encrypted reasoning
  items and message items are only replayed `if isinstance(..., list)`, so
  the Codex reasoning chain and the prefix-cache items are gone.
* `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py:1296` — reasoning-detail extraction only
  looks at `isinstance(detail, dict)` entries; a string yields nothing.
* `agent/conversation_loop.py:823` deliberately keeps `reasoning_details` on
  outbound messages ("OpenRouter uses this for multi-turn reasoning
  context") — so the forked session sends the double-encoded string to the
  provider, a shape no provider ever produced.

## Reproduction

From the repo root:

```python
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from hermes_state import SessionDB

db = SessionDB(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "state.db")
db.create_session("src", source="cli")
db.append_message(
    "src",
    role="assistant",
    content="done",
    reasoning_details=[{"type": "reasoning.text", "text": "step one"}],
    codex_reasoning_items=[{"id": "rs_1", "type": "reasoning", "encrypted_content": "blob"}],
)

# What POST /api/sessions/{id}/fork does:
db.create_session("fork", source="cli")
db.replace_messages("fork", db.get_messages("src"))

src_msg = db.get_messages_as_conversation("src")[0]
fork_msg = db.get_messages_as_conversation("fork")[0]
print("src  reasoning_details:", type(src_msg["reasoning_details"]).__name__)
print("fork reasoning_details:", type(fork_msg["reasoning_details"]).__name__)
print("fork value:", repr(fork_msg["reasoning_details"])[:80])
print("fork codex_reasoning_items:", type(fork_msg["codex_reasoning_items"]).__name__)
```

Output on current main (30e947e0a):

```
src  reasoning_details: list
fork reasoning_details: str
fork value: '[{"type": "reasoning.text", "text": "step one"}]'
fork codex_reasoning_items: str
```

The source session keeps working; only the fork is corrupted, which makes
this easy to miss in testing.

## Impact

Forked sessions silently lose all reasoning replay: preserved thinking
blocks (Anthropic), encrypted reasoning + prefix-cache message items
(Codex/Responses API), multi-turn reasoning context (OpenRouter). The DB row
still looks populated and nothing warns, so the degradation is invisible —
the fork just reasons worse than the session it branched from. Any other
caller that reuses the `get_messages()` → `replace_messages()` shape hits
the identical trap.

## Suggested Fix

Teach the two writers that these fields arrive either as live structures or
as the column's own TEXT: a small shared guard that stores strings as-is and
dumps everything else, applied at the six `json.dumps` sites in
`append_message` and `_insert_message_rows`. Live-runtime writes with
structured values serialize exactly as before, and the read path
(`get_messages`, `get_messages_as_conversation`, the GET messages endpoint,
exports) stays byte-for-byte unchanged.

The alternative — hydrating the reasoning columns in `get_messages()` the
way `content`/`tool_calls` are — would also fix the fork, but it changes the
shape returned by the GET API endpoint, session export and session search,
which feels too wide for this bug.

## Files

- `hermes_state.py`
  - `append_message` — unguarded dumps at lines 3128, 3132, 3136
  - `_insert_message_rows` — unguarded dumps at lines 3236, 3239, 3242
  - `get_messages` (line 3399) — returns the reasoning columns as raw TEXT
  - `get_messages_as_conversation` — single decode at lines 3798, 3804, 3810
- `gateway/platforms/api_server.py` — the fork round-trip at lines 1835-1836

I have the fix + regression tests ready as a follow-up PR.

labels.name: comp/agent

items.body:
## Bug Description

When the Mixture of Agents (MoA) provider is used on a platform with streaming consumers (e.g. Telegram gateway), every API call fails with `APIConnectionError: Connection error` after 3 retries.

The CLI works fine — it uses the non-streaming path which has a dedicated `elif agent.provider == "moa"` branch. The streaming path (`interruptible_streaming_api_call`) does not.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a MoA preset in config.yaml
2. Switch to MoA on a gateway platform: `/model <preset> --provider moa`
3. Send a message
4. Every request fails, logs show:

```
⚠️  API call failed (attempt 3/3): APIConnectionError
   🔌 Provider: moa  Model: codexmanager
   🌐 Endpoint: moa://local
   📝 Error: Connection error.
❌ API failed after 3 retries — Connection error.
```

## Root Cause

`agent/chat_completion_helpers.py` — `interruptible_streaming_api_call()` dispatches based on `api_mode`:

```python
if agent.api_mode == "anthropic_messages":
    ...
else:
    result["response"] = _call_chat_completions()
```

MoA has `api_mode = "chat_completions"` so it falls to `_call_chat_completions()`, which creates an OpenAI client with `agent.base_url = "moa://local"` — a virtual URL with no server.

The non-streaming path (`interruptible_api_call`) handles this correctly:

```python
elif agent.provider == "moa":
    result["response"] = agent.client.chat.completions.create(**api_kwargs)
```

## Fix

Add the same MoA branch in the streaming `_call()` (before the `else`):

```python
elif agent.provider == "moa":
    result["response"] = agent.client.chat.completions.create(**api_kwargs)
```

The MoA facade (`MoAChatCompletions.create()`) already supports streaming — it passes `stream=True` through to `call_llm()` for the aggregator.

## Temporary Workaround

Patch `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py` to add the `elif agent.provider == "moa"` branch in the streaming `_call()` function.

### Bug Description

# Summary

I found what appears to be a process lifecycle bug in Hermes' MCP reconnect logic.

Whenever the Feishu MCP server reconnects (keepalive failure, manual retry, scheduled task, or reconnect), Hermes starts a new `lark-mcp` process, but the previous process is never terminated.

Over time, multiple `lark-mcp` instances remain alive simultaneously, causing Node.js process accumulation and increasing memory usage.

### Steps to Reproduce

# Environment

**Operating System**

* macOS

**Hermes Components**

* Hermes Gateway (LaunchAgent)
* Hermes Web UI
* Hermes Bridge

**Connected Clients**

* Hermes Web UI (always running)
* Claude Code (via Hermes)
* Codex
* Feishu
* WeChat
* QQ Bot
* Composio

---

# Usage Pattern

Hermes is intended to run continuously.

Typical usage includes:

* Hermes Web UI always open
* Claude Code connected
* Codex connected
* Feishu connected
* WeChat connected
* QQ Bot connected
* Composio connected

In addition:

* Scheduled Feishu tasks run several times per day.
* I occasionally test Feishu connectivity manually.
* If a push fails, I manually retry the push.

This is normal daily usage rather than any stress test.


### Expected Behavior

Whenever Hermes reconnects to an MCP server:

```
Stop old MCP
↓

Wait until process exits
↓

Start new MCP
```

Only **one Feishu MCP instance** should exist at any time.

### Actual Behavior



Hermes behaves like this:

```
Start new MCP
↓

New MCP becomes active
↓

Old MCP remains alive
```

Every reconnect creates another pair of processes:

```
npm exec @larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp
↓

node lark-mcp
```

Old processes are never cleaned up.

Eventually multiple independent MCP processes remain running.



### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell
Hermes:
- Running as LaunchAgent (ai.hermes.gateway)
- Hermes Web UI kept running continuously

Connected clients:
- Hermes Web UI
- Claude Code
- Codex

Enabled platforms:
- Feishu
- WeChat
- QQ Bot
- Composio

Problem:
After Hermes has been running for some time, the number of `lark-mcp` processes keeps increasing.

Every time Hermes reconnects the Feishu MCP (after a keepalive failure), a new `lark-mcp` process is started, but the previous process is never terminated.

Observed process count:

2 -> 4 -> 8 -> ...

The leaked processes remain alive indefinitely.

Evidence:
- `mcp-stderr.log` shows repeated:
  starting MCP server 'feishu'
- `gateway.error.log` contains:
  WARNING tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'feishu' keepalive failed, triggering reconnect
- `ps` confirms multiple `lark-mcp` parent/child process pairs remain alive simultaneously.

I have attached:
- mcp-stderr.log
- gateway.log
- gateway.error.log
- process listings (`ps`)
- launchctl output
```

### Operating System

macOS 15.7.7

### Python Version

3.11.5

### Hermes Version

hermes web-ui v0.6.23;Hermes Agent v0.17.0

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
1. Keep Hermes Web UI running.
2. Enable Feishu MCP.
3. Use scheduled Feishu tasks and occasionally send test Feishu messages.
4. After Hermes reconnects the Feishu MCP, monitor:

pgrep -af lark-mcp

or

ps -axo pid,ppid,etime,rss,command | grep lark-mcp

The number of processes keeps increasing over time.
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

---

# Suspected Root Cause

The reconnect logic appears to create a new MCP subprocess without cleaning up the previous subprocess.

Possible causes include:

* child process not terminated
* process handle lost
* reconnect path skips cleanup
* subprocess exit not awaited

---








### Proposed Fix (optional)

Whenever Hermes reconnects to an MCP server:

```
Stop old MCP
↓

Wait until process exits
↓

Start new MCP
```

Only **one Feishu MCP instance** should exist at any time.



---





# Temporary Workaround

```
pkill -f "lark-mcp"
```

kills all leaked MCP processes.

However, they appear again after the next reconnect.



# Reproduction

The issue is reproducible.

1. Start Hermes Gateway.
2. Enable Feishu MCP.
3. Keep Hermes running.
4. Use scheduled Feishu tasks or manually send Feishu messages.
5. Trigger reconnects (manual retry, keepalive failure, scheduled tasks).

Observe:

```
pgrep -af lark-mcp
```

The number of processes continuously increases.

---

# Additional Observations

While investigating, I also observed:

* QQ reconnects normally every ~30 minutes and resumes its WebSocket session correctly.
* Hermes Gateway itself remains stable throughout the entire test.
* The leaked processes are specifically `lark-mcp` instances associated with Feishu MCP reconnects.
* The issue becomes more apparent in long-running deployments where Hermes stays online for hours or days and scheduled tasks or manual retries occur regularly.

---

items.body:
### Bug Description

Content appended by a `transform_llm_output` plugin hook is silently dropped when Hermes CLI streams a response token-by-token. The appended content is present in the final response text and stored in conversation history, but the user never sees it on screen.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install a plugin that implements `transform_llm_output` and appends a suffix to the response (e.g. a disclaimer, citation, or additional content).
2. Run `hermes` in interactive CLI mode (streaming enabled by default).
3. Send any message that triggers the plugin to append content.
4. Observe that only the streamed response is shown — the appended content is missing from the terminal output.

To confirm the content is actually there: check conversation history or run in a non-streaming surface (Dashboard, Desktop, TUI). The appended content appears correctly on all non-streaming surfaces.

### Expected Behavior

After streaming completes and `transform_llm_output` fires, any content the plugin appended to the response should be printed to the terminal.

### Actual Behavior

The CLI enters the `already_streamed` branch after streaming and skips all output with `pass`. Since `transform_llm_output` fires after the stream is closed, the plugin's appended content is never displayed.

Relevant code in `cli.py`:
```python
elif already_streamed:
    # Response was already streamed token-by-token with box framing;
    # _flush_stream() already closed the box. Skip Rich Panel.
    pass  # ← appended content is silently dropped here
```

### Root Cause Analysis

The sequence is:

1. CLI streams response token-by-token and sets `already_streamed = True`.
2. After the tool loop, `finalize_turn()` fires `transform_llm_output` hooks.
3. A plugin appends content, returning the full new response string.
4. `finalize_turn()` returns the transformed response in the result dict.
5. Back in the CLI, the `already_streamed` branch executes `pass` — the transformed response with appended content is discarded from the display path.

The fix requires two small changes:

**`agent/turn_finalizer.py`** — capture the pre-transform response so the CLI knows what was already streamed:

```python
_pre_transform_response = None

# ... inside the transform loop ...
for _hook_result in _transform_results:
    if isinstance(_hook_result, str) and _hook_result:
```

## Bug

When the dashboard is bound to a non-loopback address (e.g. `0.0.0.0`) with the **basic auth** (username/password) provider configured, navigating to `/auth/login?provider=basic` returns a **500 Internal Server Error**.

### Root cause

The `/auth/login` route handler in `hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/routes.py` calls `p.start_login()` unconditionally. However, password-only providers like `BasicAuthProvider` raise `NotImplementedError` from `start_login()` because they don't support the OAuth redirect flow — they use a POST to `/auth/password-login` instead.

### Reproduction

1. Configure basic auth in `~/.hermes/.env`:
   ```
   HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_USERNAME=admin
   HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD=secret
   HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_SECRET=$(openssl rand -base64 32)
   ```
2. Start dashboard bound to non-loopback:
   ```bash
   hermes dashboard --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9119 --no-open
   ```
3. Navigate to `http://<host>:9119/auth/login?provider=basic`
4. **Expected:** Redirect to `/login` page
5. **Actual:** 500 Internal Server Error

```
NotImplementedError: BasicAuthProvider is password-only; there is no OAuth redirect flow. The login page POSTs to /auth/password-login instead.
```

### Fix

Check `supports_password` before calling `start_login()`, and redirect to `/login` with 303 so the client can POST to `/auth/password-login`:

```python
# In /auth/login route handler, after the supports_session check:
if getattr(p, "supports_password", False):
    safe_next = _validate_post_login_target(next)
    return RedirectResponse(
        url=f"/login{'?next=' + next if safe_next else ''}",
        status_code=303,
    )
```

### Testing

- `/auth/login?provider=basic` → 303 redirect to `/login` ✅
- POST `/auth/password-login` with correct credentials → 200 ✅
- POST `/auth/password-login` with wrong credentials → 401 ✅

### Impact

This affects all users who use the basic auth provider with a non-loopback dashboard binding (Tailscale, LAN, remote backend, Hermes Desktop). The fix is backwards compatible — OAuth providers continue to work unchanged.


### Patch

```diff
diff --git a/hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/routes.py b/hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/routes.py
index 568a11957..38766da68 100644
--- a/hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/routes.py
+++ b/hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/routes.py
@@ -193,6 +193,15 @@ async def auth_login(request: Request, provider: str, next: str = ""):
             detail=f"Provider does not support interactive login: {provider!r}",
         )
 
+    # Password-only providers don't support OAuth redirect — redirect
+    # client back to the login page so it can POST to /auth/password-login.
+    if getattr(p, "supports_password", False):
+        safe_next = _validate_post_login_target(next)
+        return RedirectResponse(
+            url=f"/login{'?next=' + next if safe_next else ''}",
+            status_code=303,
+        )
+
     try:
         ls = p.start_login(redirect_uri=_redirect_uri(request))
     except ProviderError as e:

```

items.body:
## Bug Description

When multiple tool calls are dispatched in parallel within the same turn, the `context` field (the human-readable label shown in the TUI/desktop UI) gets assigned to the wrong tool call. Specifically, a failed tool call displays the context label from a *different* concurrent tool call instead of its own.

This causes confusing UI output where, for example, a "Reading .zshrc" failure badge is displayed for a `.bash_profile` read that simply returned "File not found."

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Make two `read_file` calls in parallel in the same assistant turn — one targeting an existing file, one targeting a non-existent file
2. Observe the TUI/desktop tool progress display
3. The failed call shows the context label of the successful call

Example parallel calls:
```json
// Call A — file does not exist
read_file(path="~/.bash_profile")

// Call B — file exists
read_file(path="~/.zshrc")
```

## Expected Behavior

Each tool call's `context` field should match its own `path` argument:

```json
// Call A
{"context": "Reading .bash_profile", "path": "~/.bash_profile"}

// Call B  
{"context": "Reading .zshrc", "path": "~/.zshrc"}
```

## Actual Behavior

The failed call's `context` shows the *other* call's label:

```json
// Call A (failed)
{"context": "Reading .zshrc", "path": "~/.bash_profile"}

// Call B (succeeded)
{"context": "Reading .zshrc", "path": "~/.zshrc"}
```

Both calls display "Reading .zshrc" in the UI, even though Call A was reading `.bash_profile`.

## Affected Component

- [x] Tools
- [x] Agent Core

## Investigation Notes

Traced the code path through:
- `tui_gateway/server.py` → `_tool_ctx()` (line 3193) → `build_tool_label()` from `agent/display.py`
- `agent/tool_executor.py` → `execute_tool_calls_concurrent` → pre-flight loop (lines 504–523) calls `tool_start_callback` for each tool
- `tools/file_tools.py` — `read_file` does NOT set `context`; it's a UI-layer field

The `context` field is set exclusively in the TUI/gateway layer at `server.py` line 3351:
```python
"context": _tool_ctx(name, args),
```

**Most likely root cause:** `_redact_tool_args_for_display()` in `agent/tool_executor.py` (line 396) returns the same `args` dict reference when no redaction is needed. If parallel tool calls share a mutable `args` dict (or if the pre-flight loop's iteration variable is captured by reference in a closure), one tool's args can bleed into another's context label.

Secondary suspect: the `tool_start_callback` closure in `_agent_cjs` (server.py line 3603) may capture mutable state that's overwritten before the event is emitted.

## Debug Report

Run `hermes debug share` and paste the links here:

## Operating System

macOS 27.0 (arm64)

## Hermes Version

Output of `hermes version`:

## Python Version

Python 3.11.15

## Additional Context

- The bug is UI-only — the tool result payload sent to the model (`make_tool_result_message` in `agent/tool_dispatch_helpers.py`) does NOT include a `context` field, so the LLM sees correct results
- The contamination is visible in both the TUI and the desktop app
- Both calls completed in ~120ms, so the race window is very tight

items.title: [Bug]: cronjob action='run' silently drops the per-run prompt — no context reaches the triggered job
items.body:
# [Bug]: `cronjob action='run'` silently drops the per-run `prompt` — no context reaches the triggered job

## Summary

When you trigger a cron job manually with `cronjob(action='run', job_id=..., prompt="...run-specific context...")`, the `prompt` argument is **silently discarded**. The job executes its **stored** prompt only; the per-run context never reaches the spawned session.

This is **distinct from #21867** (which is "`run` doesn't execute at all when no gateway ticker is running"). On a build that HAS the inline-execute fix (`_execute_job_now`, referenced as the "#41037 case"), the job *does* fire — but it fires **blind**, with none of the context passed on the `run` call. So #21867 = "doesn't run"; this = "runs, but throws away the run-time prompt."

## Root cause (confirmed by reading the code)

`tools/cronjob_tools.py`, the `run`/`run_now`/`trigger` branch (~line 742):

```python
if normalized in {"run", "run_now", "trigger"}:
    exec_result = _execute_job_now(job)   # <-- only the STORED job is passed
```

`_execute_job_now(job)` (~line 524) → `run_one_job(job)` (from `cron.scheduler`). The chain only ever carries the persisted job dict. The `prompt` parameter accepted by the `cronjob(...)` tool signature (line ~572) is used for `create` and `update`, but on `run` it is never read — there is no per-run context-injection path anywhere in the manual-run chain.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a recurring job whose stored prompt says "use the parameters passed in the trigger context":
   ```
   cronjob(action='create', name='ctx-test', schedule='0 9 1 1 *',
           prompt='Echo back any run parameters you were given in the trigger context. If none, say NONE.')
   ```
2. Trigger it WITH a prompt:
   ```
   cronjob(action='run', job_id='<id>', prompt='CONTEXT: client=Foo, count=3')
   ```
3. Read the job's run output.

**Observed:** the session reports it received NO context (`NONE`) — the `CONTEXT: client=Foo, count=3` never arrived.
**Expected:** the run-time `prompt` should be appended to / merged with the stored prompt (or otherwise made available to the spawned session), so a parameterized on-demand trigger can pass run-specific data.

## Impact

Any workflow that uses a far-future recurring job as an **on-demand, parameterized worker** (a common pattern: a model-pinned job you trigger with different inputs each time) cannot pass those inputs. The job either runs on stale/empty context or has to no-op. Workaround today is a side-channel (write params to a scratch file the job reads), which works but is unobvious and easy to get wrong.

## Suggested fix

In the `run` branch, thread the tool's `prompt` (when provided) into execution as a per-run context addendum — e.g. `_execute_job_now(job, extra_context=prompt)` → `run_one_job(job, extra_context=...)`, appended to the assembled prompt for that single fire only (not persisted to the job). Must stay a no-op when `prompt` is omitted, and must not alter the scheduled-tick or external-provider fire paths (keep `run_one_job`'s shared body identical for those callers).

## Environment

- OS: macOS 26.5.1
- Invocation: Hermes desktop GUI (TUI session)
- Model: anthropic/claude-opus-4.8 via openrouter
- Affected: `tools/cronjob_tools.py` (run branch), `cron/scheduler.py` (`run_one_job`)
- Note: the build here already has the inline-execute fix (`_execute_job_now`), so this is the *residual* context-passing gap, not the "doesn't run" symptom of #21867.

items.title: Honcho client is a per-process singleton — timeout config changes ignored until process restart

labels.name: area/memory
labels.description: Memory subsystem: store, providers, sync, background reviews

items.body:
## Bug description

`get_honcho_client()` in `plugins/memory/honcho/client.py` caches the Honcho SDK client in a process-wide `SingletonSlot` and returns the cached instance on every subsequent call (`client.py:788-791`), before any config resolution. The HTTP timeout is baked into the client at first build. As a result, changing the Honcho request timeout (via `~/.honcho/config.json` `timeout`, `honcho.timeout` in config.yaml, or `HONCHO_TIMEOUT`) has **no effect on any already-running process** — only freshly-spawned processes pick it up.

## Impact

Long-lived processes (the `hermes dashboard` process, the gateway launchd agents) built their client early with the default `_DEFAULT_HTTP_TIMEOUT = 30.0` (`client.py:215`). After raising the timeout to 300s to accommodate a slow local Honcho backend (self-hosted, CPU embedder), those processes kept timing out dialectic queries at 30s:

```
WARNING plugins.memory.honcho.session: Honcho dialectic query failed: Request timed out after 30.0s
```

while a fresh subprocess using the identical config correctly used 300s. The only fix was restarting every long-lived process — non-obvious, since the config was demonstrably correct.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.17.0 / v2026.6.19 (`97388704`)
- honcho-ai SDK 2.0.1, self-hosted local Honcho
- macOS 26.4, Apple Silicon

## Suggested fix

Either (a) re-read the timeout on each `get_honcho_client()` call and update the cached client's transport if it changed, or (b) document explicitly that Honcho client/config changes require a process restart (and have `hermes honcho ...` config commands print that reminder). Option (a) is friendlier since the other Honcho settings resolve per-call already.

items.body:
## Summary

When an MCP server subprocess (e.g. `mcp-remote`) fails to connect (token expiry, port contention, timeout), Hermes spawns a new process pair on retry but **never kills the previous failed processes**. This leads to rapid zombie accumulation — observed 11 orphan processes (5 failed attempts × 2 procs each + 1 latest) all competing for the same port.

## Reproduction

1. Configure an MCP server using `npx mcp-remote` (stdio subprocess mode)
2. Let the connection fail (easiest: let OAuth token expire, or block the port)
3. Trigger reconnection via `/reload-mcp` or circuit-breaker auto-recovery
4. Observe with `pgrep -fa "mcp-remote"` — previous process pairs are never terminated

## Expected Behavior

Before spawning a new MCP subprocess, Hermes should:
1. Track the PID(s) of the current subprocess for each MCP server
2. Send SIGTERM (then SIGKILL after timeout) to the old process tree before starting a new one
3. Optionally: detect port contention as a signal that an orphan is still running

## Actual Behavior

- Failed subprocesses remain running indefinitely
- Each holds the configured port open, causing subsequent spawns to also fail (port already in use)
- Cascading failure: each retry adds 2 more zombies (npm parent + node child)
- Only workaround is manual: `pkill -9 -f "mcp-remote"` then `/reload-mcp`

## Impact

- Port exhaustion makes reconnection impossible without manual intervention
- Memory/CPU waste from idle zombie processes
- Particularly bad with token-expiry-triggered circuit breaker recovery, which can retry multiple times in quick succession

## Environment

- macOS (Hermes TUI)
- MCP server: `npx mcp-remote` (v0.1.37) connecting to Salesforce
- Hermes Agent (latest)

## Suggested Fix

In the MCP server lifecycle manager:
- Maintain a `pid` reference per configured MCP server
- On reconnect/reload: kill the existing process group (`process.kill(-pid)` or `SIGTERM` + `SIGKILL` fallback) before spawning the replacement
- Consider a process group (`setsid`) wrapper so the entire tree can be killed cleanly

```
    from distutils.version import StrictVersion
```

labels.name: comp/cli

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

User-installed plugins as symlinks (e.g. `~/.hermes/plugins/my-plugin -> ~/projects/my-plugin`) are silently rejected by the plugin discovery and `hermes plugins enable` after the path-traversal security fix (commit `7cff95644`, PR #46435).

The `_sanitize_plugin_name` guard calls `.resolve()` on the plugin path before checking `relative_to(plugins_dir)`. Because `.resolve()` follows symlinks, the resolved path points outside `~/.hermes/plugins/` and the guard raises `ValueError: resolves outside the plugins directory` — even though the symlink entry itself lives inside the plugins directory.

## Steps to Reproduce

```bash
# Create a plugin in a development location
mkdir -p ~/projects/my-plugin/dashboard
echo '{}' > ~/projects/my-plugin/dashboard/manifest.json

# Install as symlink (common developer workflow)
ln -s ~/projects/my-plugin ~/.hermes/plugins/my-plugin

# Plugin is not discovered
hermes plugins list --plain --no-bundled
# Output: only shows plugins that are real directories, not symlinks

# Trying to enable fails
hermes plugins enable my-plugin
# Error: Plugin 'my-plugin' is not installed or bundled.
```

## Expected Behavior

Symlinks in `~/.hermes/plugins/` that point to a valid plugin directory should be discovered and enableable. The path-traversal guard should check whether the **symlink entry itself** lives inside `plugins_dir`, not its resolved target.

## Actual Behavior

Symlinks are silently skipped during discovery and fail with "not installed or bundled" when explicitly enabled.

## Root Cause

`_sanitize_plugin_name` in `hermes_cli/plugins_cmd.py` (line ~120):

```python
target = (plugins_dir / name).resolve()   # follows symlink → escapes plugins_dir
plugins_resolved = plugins_dir.resolve()
target.relative_to(plugins_resolved)       # raises ValueError
```

Fix: check that the **symlink itself** is inside `plugins_dir` before resolving — or use `Path.is_symlink()` to allow direct (non-traversal) symlinks that live inside `plugins_dir`.

```python
entry = plugins_dir / name
# Allow symlinks that live directly inside plugins_dir (no traversal in name)
if entry.is_symlink():
    return entry  # symlink itself is inside plugins_dir; target is operator's choice
target = entry.resolve()
# ... existing relative_to check for non-symlink paths
```

## Environment

- Hermes version: personal/oauth-bypass-billing-restriction (rebased on main `ff8cf56a0`)
- macOS 26.5.1
- Regression introduced by commit `7cff95644` (fix(dashboard): gate plugin asset serving and API mount on plugins.enabled)

## Workaround

Replace symlinks with real clones via `hermes plugins install file:///<path>` — but this breaks the live-edit developer workflow where the plugin repo is the authoritative source.

## Bug Description

When using MoA (Mixture of Agents) with the GitHub Copilot provider, non-GPT reference models (Claude, Gemini) fail with HTTP 400:

```
Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'model claude-sonnet-4.6 does not support Responses API.', 'code': 'unsupported_api_for_model'}}
Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'model gemini-3.1-pro-preview does not support Responses API.', 'code': 'unsupported_api_for_model'}}
```

GPT-5.4 works correctly as a reference model.

## Root Cause

`copilot_request_headers()` in `hermes_cli/copilot_auth.py` unconditionally includes:
```python
"Openai-Intent": "conversation-edits"
```

This header tells the GitHub Copilot gateway to route ALL requests through the Responses API server-side, regardless of the client endpoint being called (`/chat/completions`). Non-GPT models do not support the Responses API and are rejected.

The model routing logic in `_should_use_copilot_responses_api()` and `copilot_model_api_mode()` correctly identifies which models need Responses API (GPT-5+ only), but this information is not propagated to the header generation.

## Expected Behavior

MoA reference calls to Claude and Gemini models should succeed via `/chat/completions` without triggering Responses API routing.

## Suggested Fix

Make the `Openai-Intent: conversation-edits` header conditional on the model supporting the Responses API. Pass the resolved model name to `copilot_request_headers()` and only include the header for GPT-5+ models (using the same logic as `_should_use_copilot_responses_api()`).

The call site in `resolve_provider_client()` (`agent/auxiliary_client.py` ~line 4440) already has access to `final_model`.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.18.0 (2026.7.1)
- Provider: GitHub Copilot (corporate subscription)
- MoA config: 3 reference models (claude-sonnet-4.6, gemini-3.5-flash, gpt-5.4)
- OpenAI SDK: 2.24.0

## Workaround

Use only GPT-family models as MoA references (loses model-family diversity which defeats MoA purpose).

---
*This issue was filed with AI assistance using Hermes Agent (claude-opus-4.6).*

## Summary
Model selector dropdown crashes with `'dict' object has no attribute 'lower'`.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open Hermes Desktop on macOS.
2. Click the model selector in the bottom input bar (`Step 3.7 Flash:Free ...`).
3. The dropdown panel shows an error message instead of the model list:
   `'dict' object has no attribute 'lower'`.

## Expected Behavior
The model list should load and allow switching models.

## Actual Behavior
The dropdown shows an error stub and the model list cannot be switched.

## Environment
- OS: macOS (Apple Silicon)
- Version: # v0.18.0 (`ed41237`)

## Notes
- Issue appears to be in the model list rendering code.
- `model_catalog.enabled` is `true` in config.
- Config file ( `model` / `providers` / `model_catalog` ) looks valid in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`.
- This prevents normal model switching in the desktop app UI.
- Use-case workaround: falling back to other clients while this is fixed.
